rules.description: Every call returns one well-formed decision for each application received that day (approved amount a whole number from 1,000 to the requested amount, 0 otherwise) and none for anything else; a call that fails or times out breaks it too.

Every call returns a limit table with a number for every customer who has applied in the period so far (that day included), the daily capacity left and, from medium, the period budget left; the desk and treasury work from it.
Applications of customers with an active delinquency are declined.
Approvals only when the policy bureau's score (bureau_a_score) is at least 745.

What a customer is approved on a day (all their applications together) is at most their customer limit that morning, min(50,000, 65% of annual income, DSR headroom at 35%) minus our approvals to them earlier in the period. It never bends, since the income cap is regulatory and so is the DSR cap from medium (medium+, the cap moves by the regulator's notice from its effective date; hard, repayments and verified income count); in easy the DSR cap is our own affordability limit on installment loans, with no exception, and the regulator's notice does not reach it.
The amount approved on one day is at most the daily disbursement capacity of 250,000 (our funding line).

No day's approvals take the amount approved in the period above the period budget in force that day, 3,400,000 (400,000 less from the treasury's budget cut); a cut below what is already approved stops further approvals but does not undo earlier ones.

Every decline carries the code of its main driver after the day's approvals, the first that applies of DELINQUENCY, LOW_SCORE, SPLIT_APPLICATION (hard), LIMIT_EXCEEDED (less than 1,000 of customer limit left), CREDIT_RISK.
Age band, gender and nationality never influence a decision; planted twin applications that differ only in them get the same decision and amount.
At least 30% of the total amount approved over the period goes to near-prime customers (bureau_a_score below 840), a commitment to the regulator.
Beyond the referrals the rules require (the tenure habit; in hard also the income-discrepancy procedure), at most 3 applications are referred on a day (the underwriters' capacity).
Applicants with fewer than 3 months in their current job are referred to a human underwriter (unless declined for delinquency); a habit the head of credit can grant exceptions to.
